mainTopic: How בדיקת חמץ is done: with a נר, in which places, and its limits because of danger
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא that says we search for חמץ only by the light of a נר, and it brings verses as a זכר לדבר. The גמרא asks where the ban on searching by sunlight applies. It concludes that it means the sides of a room lit by a skylight (ארובה). Next it asks why a torch (אבוקה) is not allowed, since it is brighter. Four אמוראים each explain why a נר is still better for searching. The גמרא then explains which places need no בדיקה. It settles clashing ברייתות about holes, beds, and storerooms: a place needs checking only if a person might bring חמץ there, for example in the middle of a meal. Finally, a ברייתא excuses a person from reaching into holes because of danger. This leads to the 'dog test' for buried חמץ and to a discussion of שלוחי מצוה אינן ניזוקין, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The reason a lamp is used for searching
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that we search for חמץ only by a נר because its light is well suited for searching.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the light of a lamp is good for searching.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of the ברייתא's ruling, which began on the previous עמוד. It gives the reason why only a נר, and not sun, moon, or torch, is used for בדיקת חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא listed three light sources you may NOT use and one you must use. Here it explains the positive side: a נר's light is effective for searching. It can be brought into holes and cracks and gives a focused light.

keyTerms.meaning: The light of a lamp or candle

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the END of a ברייתא that started on the previous עמוד (7b): 'We do not search by sunlight, moonlight, or a torch, only by a lamp.' The later questions about אור החמה and אבוקה refer back to that earlier part.

phrases.english: because the light of a lamp is good for searching.
phrases.notes: Concludes the ruling of the ברייתא begun on 7b.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continuation of the ברייתא from the previous עמוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בדיקת חמץ is done by the light of a נר because its light is effective for searching.

steps.title: Verses hinting that searching is done with a lamp
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא admits there is no real proof, but brings a chain of four פסוקים as a hint (זכר לדבר) linking חמץ, searching, and lamps.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though there is no proof for this, there is a hint for it. It says: 'Seven days, leaven shall not be found in your houses.' It also says: 'And he searched, starting with the eldest.' It also says: 'At that time I will search Jerusalem with lamps.' And it also says: 'The lamp of ה׳ is the soul of man, searching all the inner chambers.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא supports the use of a נר with verses. It is careful to call them only a 'hint,' not a true proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verses work like a chain. 'Not be found' (ימצא) links to 'found' in the story of יוסף's goblet, where the word 'searched' (ויחפש) appears. 'Search' then links to the verse in צפניה, 'I will search Jerusalem with lamps.' The last verse in משלי shows that the searching is done with a נר, a single lamp, not a torch.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no (real) proof for the matter
A hint/allusion to the matter (weaker than a proof)
And it (the verse) says, introducing an additional verse

steps.whyThisMatters: The phrase זכר לדבר tells us the use of a נר is not learned from a binding derivation. The verses are only a supporting allusion.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר —
phrases.english: And even though there is no proof for the matter,
there is an allusion to the matter, as it is stated:
"Seven days leaven shall not be found in your houses,"
phrases.notes: שמות יב:יט. The key word is 'found.'

phrases.english: and it says: "And he searched, starting with the eldest,"
phrases.notes: בראשית מד:יב. The goblet was 'found,' and the word 'searched' appears.

phrases.english: and it says: "At that time I will search
phrases.notes: צפניה א:יב

phrases.english: Jerusalem with lamps,"
and it says: "The lamp of God is the soul of man,
phrases.notes: משלי כ:כז

phrases.english: searching all the inward parts."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר זֵכֶר לַדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides scriptural allusion for the ruling just stated.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that בדיקת חמץ is done with a נר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A chain of verses linked by shared words (ימצא, חיפוש, נרות), ending with 'נר ה׳ ... חופש.'

steps.title: What case of sunlight is the ברייתא talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exact situation the ברייתא means when it rules out searching by sunlight.
steps.simpleTranslation: This 'light of the sun,' what case are we talking about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back to the ברייתא's first exclusion, 'not by sunlight,' and asks where this would apply. This sets up the next moves, where the גמרא will test possible locations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling sounds strange, because sunlight is very bright. So the גמרא wants to pin down a place where sunlight would reach but still not be good enough. It is about to test several options.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?

phrases.english: This light of the sun, what are the circumstances?
phrases.notes: Refers back to 'אין בודקין לאור החמה' in the ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the opening clause of the ברייתא to define its case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what location does the prohibition of searching by sunlight apply?

steps.title: It cannot mean a courtyard
steps.stepSummary: If the case were a חצר, that makes no sense, because רבא says a חצר does not need בדיקה at all, since birds eat any חמץ there.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means in a courtyard, didn't רבא say that a courtyard doesn't need searching, because ravens are found there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option, a חצר, and rejects it using a statement of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A courtyard is in full sunlight, so it seems like a natural case. But רבא rules that a חצר needs no search at all, because ravens and other birds will eat any חמץ left there. So the ברייתא can't be talking about which light to use in a place that needs no search.

keyTerms.meaning: Ravens (birds that eat food left out)
But didn't [he] say? (introduces a contradicting statement)

phrases.english: If we say it is in a courtyard,

phrases.aramaic: הָאָמַר רָבָא: חָצֵר אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה בְּדִיקָה,
phrases.english: but didn't Rava say: a courtyard does not require searching,
because ravens are commonly found there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first candidate case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the sunlight case is a חצר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חצר needs no בדיקה at all (רבא), so there is no question of which light to search by.

steps.title: It cannot mean a portico either
steps.stepSummary: If the case were an אכסדרה, רבא says an אכסדרה may be searched by its own natural light, so sunlight there is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, maybe it means a portico. But didn't רבא say that a portico is searched by its own light?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second option, an אכסדרה (a roofed area open on the sides), and rejects it too with another statement of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אכסדרה is roofed, so birds don't clean it, and it does need בדיקה. But רבא says its own daylight is enough for the search. That is the opposite of the ברייתא's 'not by sunlight,' so the ברייתא can't be talking about an אכסדרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Portico: a roofed area open on one or more sides
Is searched by its own (natural) light

phrases.english: Rather, in a portico,
but didn't Rava say: a portico is searched by its own light!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the second candidate case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the sunlight case is an אכסדרה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא permits searching an אכסדרה by daylight, which contradicts the ברייתא's ban on sunlight.

steps.title: The case is a room with a skylight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is needed for a room that gets sunlight through a skylight (ארובה).
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a skylight that is in a room.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new location that avoids both problems: an indoor room lit by a skylight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A room is enclosed, so birds don't come in and it needs בדיקה, unlike a חצר. It is also not as open and bright as an אכסדרה. So the ruling 'not by sunlight' teaches that the light coming through a skylight is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for (this specific case)
Skylight, an opening in the roof

phrases.english: No, it is necessary for a skylight that is in a room.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the problem raised by steps 4 and 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-defining the case (אוקימתא) in a new location
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sunlight case seemed to have no possible location, since a חצר needs no search and an אכסדרה may use daylight.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא refers to a room lit through a skylight.

steps.title: Where in the skylight room?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which part of the room is meant. Directly under the skylight would be just like an אכסדרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where in the room? If it is right opposite the skylight, that is the same as a portico.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens the answer by asking exactly which spot in the room is meant. It rules out the spot directly under the skylight, which sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The area right under the opening gets strong, direct light, just like an אכסדרה, which רבא allowed to be searched by daylight. So that spot can't be what the ברייתא forbids.

phrases.english: And where?
If it is opposite the skylight,
that is the same as a portico.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְהֵיכָא אִי לְבַהֲדֵי אֲרוּבָּה הַיְינוּ אַכְסַדְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refines the answer of step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which part of the skylight room is the ברייתא referring to?

steps.title: The sides of the room
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means the sides of the room, which do not get direct light from the skylight.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means the sides.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the ban on searching by sunlight applies to the side areas of a skylight room. There the indirect sunlight is too weak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sides of the room get only scattered light, which is not good enough to find crumbs in cracks. In those areas you must use a נר.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's 'not by sunlight' means the sides of a room lit by a skylight. A חצר needs no search, and an אכסדרה or the spot directly under a skylight may be searched by daylight.

phrases.english: Rather, it is to the sides.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sides of the room, away from the direct light of the skylight.

steps.title: Isn't a torch brighter than a lamp?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's ban on an אבוקה. רבא explains a פסוק to mean that צדיקים before the שכינה are like a נר before a torch, which shows a torch is far brighter.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a torch is not allowed? But didn't רבא say: what is the meaning of the verse, 'And a brightness like light shall be, rays from His hand, and there is the hiding of His power'? To what are the righteous compared before the Divine Presence? Like a lamp in front of a torch.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves to the ברייתא's exclusion of a torch. It questions it using רבא's teaching that a torch outshines a lamp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The parable compares the צדיקים to a small נר and the שכינה to a great אבוקה. This shows that a torch's light is much stronger. If brightness is what matters for searching, a torch should be even better than a lamp.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written?

steps.confusionAlert: The parable is aggadic, but the גמרא uses it to learn a practical fact: a torch gives far more light than a lamp. Steps 11-14 answer this challenge.

phrases.english: And a torch, not?
But didn't Rava say: what is that which is written:
"And a brightness shall be like the light,
phrases.notes: חבקוק ג:ד

phrases.english: rays at His side,
and there is the hiding of His power";
to what are the righteous comparable before the Divine Presence?
Like a lamp before a torch.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the sunlight exclusion to the torch exclusion in the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that one may not search by an אבוקה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא's parable shows a torch is much brighter than a lamp, so it should be at least as good for searching.

steps.title: A torch is the best choice for הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a second statement of רבא: using an אבוקה for הבדלה is the ideal way to do the מצוה, which again shows a torch's superior light.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: a torch for הבדלה is the מצוה in the best way!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא strengthens its challenge with another ruling of רבא. Even in הלכה, a torch is treated as the better light.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the ברכה of בורא מאורי האש at הבדלה, a torch is preferred because of its strong light. This makes the ברייתא's ban on a torch for בדיקת חמץ even harder to understand. The גמרא will resolve it next.

keyTerms.meaning: The ceremony ending שבת, including a blessing over fire
The מצוה done in the choicest, ideal way

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical הלכה: the ideal flame for הבדלה is a multi-wick torch. That is why many use a braided הבדלה candle.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
a torch for havdala is the מצוה in the optimal manner!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא אֲבוּקָה לְהַבְדָּלָה מִצְוָה מִן הַמּוּבְחָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, halachic source to reinforce the challenge of step 9.
steps.raayaObject: The claim underlying the קשיא that a torch's light is superior to a lamp's.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's ruling that an אבוקה is the ideal light for הבדלה.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: a candle fits into holes, a torch does not
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that the torch is not banned for being dim. It is banned because it is too big to reach into holes and cracks, while a candle can.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: This one (the candle) can be brought into holes and cracks, and that one (the torch) cannot be brought into holes and cracks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from steps 9-10. If a torch is brighter, why does the ברייתא forbid it for בדיקת חמץ? רב נחמן בר יצחק says a torch is simply too large to fit into holes and cracks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that the ברייתא banned the torch for giving weak light. This answer changes the reason. Brightness is not the issue; reach is. A small candle flame can go into the tight spots where חמץ hides, and a big torch cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: To bring it in, to insert it
A torch (a large flame with several wicks)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is NOT saying a candle gives more light than a torch. רבא already showed that a torch is brighter. The point here is that the candle is more useful for searching.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
This one (the candle) — one can bring it
phrases.notes: זה = the נר, the small candle

phrases.english: into holes and into cracks,
and that one (the torch) — one cannot bring it
phrases.notes: Second זה = the אבוקה

phrases.english: into holes and into cracks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised by רבא's two statements that a torch is brighter.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the reason: the torch is banned for being impractical, not for being dim.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the ברייתא banned the torch because it gives too little light.
steps.terutzMaskana: A torch cannot reach into holes and cracks, so a candle is better for searching.

steps.title: רב זביד: a candle's light goes forward, a torch's light goes backward
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד gives a second answer. A candle sends its light ahead toward the spot being searched, while a torch's light falls back onto the person holding it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: This one (the candle) has its light in front of it, and that one (the torch) has its light behind it.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different reason why a candle beats a torch for searching. רב זביד says it depends on which direction the light goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When you hold a candle out in front of you, the light lands on the place you are checking. A torch's light, by contrast, falls back onto the searcher instead of onto the search area. Like רב נחמן בר יצחק, he agrees the torch is brighter, but says it is less useful.

keyTerms.meaning: Its light is in front of it

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said:
This one (the candle) — its light is in front of it,
and that one (the torch) — its light is behind it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the same challenge that step 11 answered.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A brighter light should search better.
steps.terutzMaskana: The torch's light does not point toward the place being searched.

steps.title: רב פפא: with a torch, a person is afraid of starting a fire
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a third answer. Someone holding a torch is nervous about burning the house down, so he will not search carefully. With a candle he is calm.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: With this one (the torch) a person is afraid, and with that one (the candle) he is not afraid.
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא gives yet another reason. A torch makes the searcher afraid of fire, so he will not look into every corner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reason is about the searcher's state of mind, not the light itself. A person afraid of setting a fire will hurry and skip spots. Notice that here הַאי (the first 'this') means the torch, unlike the earlier answers where the first 'this' was the candle.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch the order! In רב פפא's statement, the first הַאי is the TORCH (which makes him afraid). In steps 11 and 12, the first זה was the CANDLE.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
With this one (the torch) — he is afraid (of starting a fire),
and with that one (the candle) — he is not afraid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the same challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A brighter light should search better.
steps.terutzMaskana: Fear of fire stops a person from searching carefully with a torch.

steps.title: רבינא: a candle gives steady light, a torch flickers
steps.stepSummary: רבינא gives a fourth answer. A candle's light is steady and even, while a torch's light jumps and flickers, which makes careful searching hard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: This one (the candle) gives a steady stream of light, and that one (the torch) flickers in jumps.
steps.whatsHappening: The fourth and last answer to the challenge. רבינא says a candle gives a steady light, while a torch flickers on and off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A torch may be brighter overall, but its jumping flame keeps changing what you can see, so you might miss a crumb. A steady small light is better for close, careful checking. All four answers agree on the main idea: a torch is brighter but worse for searching.
steps.whatToRemember: Four reasons a candle is better than a torch for בדיקת חמץ: (1) it fits into holes, (2) its light points forward, (3) it does not cause fear of fire, (4) its light is steady. All of them admit that a torch is brighter.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
This one (the candle) — draws light steadily,
and that one (the torch) — flickers in jumps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last of four alternative answers. This closes the torch discussion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A brighter light should search better.
steps.terutzMaskana: A flickering torch is less reliable for searching than a steady candle.

steps.title: What does the משנה's phrase 'any place' come to include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's rule that any place where חמץ is not brought needs no checking. It asks what extra cases the word 'any' (כל) adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: Any place into which חמץ is not brought (does not need checking). What does 'any place' come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the next line of the משנה and asks what the broad word 'any place' is meant to add. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא often reads the word כל ('all' or 'any') as hinting at extra cases that are not stated outright. So it asks which specific places the משנה is quietly including in 'no checking needed.'

keyTerms.meaning: What does it come to include?

phrases.english: Any place into which one does not bring (chametz), etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה: such a place does not need checking

phrases.english: 'Any place' — what does it come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: back to the משנה after the torch discussion ends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which places are included by the word 'any' in the משנה's exemption.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists places that need no checking; רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds a bed that does
steps.stepSummary: The word 'any' includes a list from a ברייתא: high and low holes, certain roofs, a cowshed, chicken coops, a straw shed, and wine and oil storerooms. None of these need checking. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds that a bed that divides a room, with space under it, does need checking.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include what רבנן taught: the upper and lower holes of a house, the roof of a porch, the roof of a closet, a cowshed, chicken coops, a straw shed, wine storerooms and oil storerooms do not need checking. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: a bed that divides the house and leaves a space under it needs checking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא lists places where people usually do not bring חמץ, so they need no checking. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל then names one place that does need checking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The listed places are either hard to reach (very high or very low holes, roofs) or used for things that have nothing to do with bread (animal sheds, storage). Since nobody brings חמץ there, no בדיקה is needed. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל worries that חמץ might roll under a raised bed, so he requires checking there.

keyTerms.meaning: The very high and very low holes in a house's walls

phrases.english: To include that which the Rabbis taught (in a ברייתא):
The upper and lower holes of a house,
and the roof of a porch, and the roof of a closet,
and a cowshed, and chicken coops, and a straw shed,
and wine storerooms and oil storerooms —
do not need checking.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
A bed that divides the inside of a house and leaves a space (under it) —
needs checking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Any place' includes the ברייתא's list of places that need no checking. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rules that a divided bed with space under it does need checking.

steps.title: A second ברייתא that seems to say the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a different ברייתא. A hole between two neighbors' houses must be checked by each neighbor as far as his hand reaches. Here רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says a dividing bed with wood and stones under it does NOT need checking.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they contrasted it with this: A hole between one person and his neighbor — this one checks as far as his hand reaches, and that one checks as far as his hand reaches, and the rest he cancels in his heart. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: a bed that divides the house, with wood and stones arranged under it, and leaves a space — does not need checking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets a second ברייתא against the first one. This step lays out the clashing source; the next step will spell out exactly where the clash is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא said holes need no checking, but this one says a hole must be checked as far as the hand can reach. The first ברייתא had רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requiring a bed to be checked, but here he says it does not need checking. Whatever is left unchecked is handled by ביטול, cancelling the חמץ in one's heart.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted it (they set one source against another)
As far as his hand reaches
He cancels it in his heart (ביטול חמץ)

phrases.english: And they contrasted it: A hole that is between a person and his neighbor —
phrases.notes: A hole in the shared wall between two houses

phrases.aramaic: זֶה בּוֹדֵק עַד מָקוֹם שֶׁיָּדוֹ מַגַּעַת,
phrases.english: this one checks as far as his hand reaches,

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶה בּוֹדֵק עַד מָקוֹם שֶׁיָּדוֹ מַגַּעַת,
phrases.english: and that one checks as far as his hand reaches,
and the rest — he cancels it in his heart.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
A bed that divides the inside of the house,
with wood and stones arranged under it,
and it leaves a space —
phrases.notes: There is a gap between the bed and the wood and stones underneath

phrases.english: does not need checking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that seems to contradict the ברייתא in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא from step 16 (its rulings on holes and on the bed).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא gives the opposite ruling on the same two cases, holes and a dividing bed.

steps.title: The double contradiction: bed against bed, holes against holes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names the two clashes outright. The two rulings about the bed contradict each other, and the two rulings about holes contradict each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difficulty: bed against bed! There is a difficulty: holes against holes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the problem it set up in step 17. The two ברייתות disagree about the bed and also about the holes. The answers will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bed: in the first ברייתא, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it needs checking; in the second, he says it does not. Holes: the first ברייתא says house holes need no checking; the second says a hole must be checked as far as the hand reaches. These are two separate questions, and each will need its own answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Bed against bed (one ruling about the bed against the other)

steps.confusionAlert: There are TWO separate contradictions here, not one. Keep them apart: (1) the bed, where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל seems to argue with himself, and (2) the holes, where the unnamed first opinions in the two ברייתות clash.
steps.whatToRemember: Two ברייתות clash on two points: the bed (check it or not, according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל) and holes (check them or not). The גמרא will need to settle both.
steps.whyThisMatters: Settling these clashes will define the practical limits of בדיקת חמץ: exactly which holes and spaces under furniture must be searched.

phrases.english: There is a difficulty: bed against bed,
there is a difficulty: holes against holes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the exact points of contradiction between the ברייתות of steps 16 and 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rulings on the bed and on holes in the two ברייתות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Bed: needs checking vs. no checking. Holes: no checking vs. check as far as the hand reaches.

steps.title: Holes: high and low ones versus middle ones
steps.stepSummary: The two ברייתות about holes do not truly clash. The one that says no checking is talking about very high or very low holes. The one that says checking is needed is talking about middle-height holes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Hole against hole is not a problem. This ruling is about upper and lower holes, and that ruling is about middle holes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the first contradiction from step 18. It shows that each ברייתא is talking about a different kind of hole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holes that are very high or very low are hard to reach, so nobody puts food in them, and they need no checking. A hole at middle height is easy to use, so חמץ may have been put there. That is why each neighbor must check it as far as his hand reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult; there is no real contradiction

phrases.english: Holes against holes is not difficult:
phrases.notes: The first contradiction named in step 18.

phrases.english: this one is about upper and lower holes,
phrases.notes: The first ברייתא (step 16): no checking, because these are hard to use.

phrases.english: and that one is about middle holes.
phrases.notes: The second ברייתא (step 17): checking is needed, because these are easy to use.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the holes half of the double contradiction in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source is about a different type of hole.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to rule on the same holes in opposite ways.
steps.terutzMaskana: Hard-to-reach high and low holes need no checking. Usable middle holes do.

steps.title: Beds: a raised bed versus a low bed
steps.stepSummary: The two rulings of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about the dividing bed do not clash. A raised bed needs checking. A low bed does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bed against bed is not a problem. This ruling is about a bed that is raised up, and that ruling is about a bed that is low.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second contradiction from step 18, again by showing that each ruling is about a different kind of bed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a bed stands high off the floor, the space under it can be used, so חמץ may be there and it must be checked. When a bed sits low, the space under it cannot be used, so no checking is needed. This fits the second ברייתא, where wood and stones are stacked under the bed and leave only a narrow gap (מפסקת) that nobody uses.

phrases.english: Bed against bed is not difficult:
phrases.notes: The second contradiction named in step 18.

phrases.english: this one is about a raised bed,
phrases.notes: The first ברייתא (step 16): checking is needed, because the space underneath is usable.

phrases.english: that one is about a low bed.
phrases.notes: The second ברייתא (step 17): no checking, because the space underneath cannot be used.

steps.whatToRemember: Both contradictions have the same answer. A place needs checking only if people actually use it. Hard-to-reach holes and the space under low beds are not used, so they need no checking.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the bed half of the double contradiction, which closes the cycle that began in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ruling is about a different height of bed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל seemed to contradict himself about the same bed.
steps.terutzMaskana: A raised bed with usable space underneath needs checking. A low bed does not.

steps.title: Another ברייתא says wine storerooms need checking
steps.stepSummary: The first ברייתא listed wine storerooms as needing no checking. The גמרא quotes a different ברייתא that says wine storerooms do need checking, though oil storerooms do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do wine storerooms really need no checking? But a ברייתא taught: wine storerooms need checking, and oil storerooms do not need checking!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge against the list from step 16. Another ברייתא says the opposite about wine storerooms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The step 16 list said wine and oil storerooms both need no checking. This new ברייתא agrees about oil but says wine storerooms do need checking. So the two sources clash only about wine.

keyTerms.meaning: but it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a contradicting source)

phrases.english: And do wine storerooms not need checking?!
phrases.notes: Refers back to the list in step 16.

phrases.english: But it was taught in a ברייתא:
wine storerooms need checking,
oil storerooms do not need checking!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the holes and beds are settled, the גמרא picks out another item from the step 16 list and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The step 16 ברייתא's ruling that wine storerooms need no checking.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא says outright that wine storerooms need checking, which contradicts the first.

steps.title: The second ברייתא means someone who refills during the meal
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that requires checking is talking about someone who goes into the wine storeroom during his meal to get more wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Someone who refills his supply from the storeroom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the clash by narrowing the case of the second ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person goes down to the wine cellar in the middle of a meal, he may carry bread in with him. So that kind of storeroom needs checking. The first ברייתא is about a storeroom nobody enters during a meal, so it needs no checking.

keyTerms.meaning: what case are we dealing with here? (a formula that narrows a source to a specific case)
one who refills his supply from the storeroom during the meal

steps.confusionAlert: מסתפק here does NOT mean 'is in doubt' (the usual meaning of ספק). It means 'takes a supply' from the storeroom while eating.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
With one who refills his supply from it during the meal.
phrases.notes: Since he may bring bread in his hand, חמץ may get into the storeroom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting one source to a specific case (אוקימתא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to discuss every wine storeroom.
steps.terutzMaskana: A wine storeroom that a person enters during meals to refill needs checking. Other wine storerooms do not.

steps.title: Then oil storerooms should need checking too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If refilling during the meal is the reason, then oil storerooms used that way should also need checking.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, oil too should need checking!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If refilling is the reason, why does the same ברייתא still say oil storerooms need no checking?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats wine and oil differently. But people also use oil at meals, so someone could go into the oil storeroom with bread too. The reason of מסתפק seems to apply equally to both.

keyTerms.meaning: if so (introduces a challenge that builds on the previous answer)

phrases.english: If so, oil storerooms too should need checking!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's distinction between wine and oil, as explained by step 22.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If refilling during the meal brings חמץ in, that should be just as true for oil as for wine.

steps.title: Oil has a set amount per meal; wine does not
steps.stepSummary: People know in advance how much oil a meal needs, so they take it beforehand. Nobody knows how much wine he will drink, so he may go back for more during the meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Oil has a fixed amount for eating. Wine has no fixed amount for drinking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the refilling reason applies to wine but not to oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since oil use is predictable, a person gets all of it before the meal starts and never enters the oil storeroom with bread in hand. Wine drinking is unpredictable, so he may run down mid-meal holding bread. This is what makes the wine storeroom a likely place for חמץ.

phrases.english: Oil has a fixed amount for eating.
phrases.notes: So a person takes what he needs before the meal begins.

phrases.english: Wine has no fixed amount for drinking.
phrases.notes: So he may go back during the meal with bread in hand.

steps.whatToRemember: A storeroom needs checking only if people enter it in the middle of a meal. Wine storerooms fit that description because wine drinking has no set amount. Oil storerooms do not, because the oil for a meal is taken beforehand.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Drawing a real-life difference between the two cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wine and oil seemed to be equally likely to be refilled during a meal.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only wine is refilled mid-meal, because its amount is unpredictable.

steps.title: Beer storerooms in Babylonia are like wine storerooms in Israel
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches that in בבל, where beer is the usual drink, beer storerooms are treated like wine storerooms in ארץ ישראל. They need checking when people refill from them during meals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: חכמים made beer storerooms in בבל like wine storerooms in ארץ ישראל, in the case of one who refills during the meal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching from רבי חייא that applies the rule just learned to a new place and a new drink.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not really about wine itself. It is about whatever drink people refill during meals without a set amount. In בבל that drink was beer, so beer storerooms take the place of wine storerooms.

keyTerms.meaning: a great teacher from the time between the תנאים and the אמוראים
beer (often made from dates or barley)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the הלכה follows how people actually behave. A local drink with no set amount, such as beer in בבל, is treated like wine.

phrases.english: רבי חייא taught:
They made beer storerooms in Babylonia
like wine storerooms in the Land of Israel,
in the case of one who refills from them during the meal.
phrases.notes: In that case they need checking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the מסתפק rule from steps 22 and 24 to beer in בבל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Beer storerooms in בבל that are entered during meals need checking, just like wine storerooms in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Fish storerooms do not need checking
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that a fish storeroom does not need בדיקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: A fish storeroom does not need checking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רב חסדא. A room where fish are stored does not need to be checked for חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the rule from the last steps: a room needs checking only if a person might go in during a meal. רב חסדא's view is that people do not go back into the fish room in the middle of a meal.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
A fish storeroom does not need checking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 'refilling during the meal' rule to another type of storeroom.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fish storeroom needs no בדיקה.

steps.title: A ברייתא says fish storerooms do need checking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא from a ברייתא that requires checking a fish storeroom.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא taught: They need checking!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא. A ברייתא says that fish storerooms do need checking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא's ruling seems to go directly against a ברייתא. The two sources look like they are arguing about the very same room.

keyTerms.meaning: but it was taught (in a ברייתא)

phrases.english: But it was taught: they need checking!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that a fish storeroom needs no בדיקה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא directly says the opposite.

steps.title: Big fish versus small fish
steps.stepSummary: Big fish need no checking. Small fish need checking because a person may refill them during the meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a contradiction. This one (no checking) is about big fish, and that one (checking) is about small fish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by splitting the case. רב חסדא is talking about big fish, and the ברייתא is talking about small fish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With big fish, a person knows ahead of time how many he needs, so he will not go back during the meal. With small fish, he cannot tell how many he will eat, so he may walk in with bread to get more. This is the same reasoning used for oil versus wine in step 24.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is about big fish,
that one is about small fish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by splitting it into two cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case (אוקימתא): each source deals with a different kind of fish.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources seemed to argue about every fish storeroom.
steps.terutzMaskana: Big fish need no checking. Small fish do, because a person may refill them during the meal.
steps.whatToRemember: The test for every storeroom is the same: might a person go in during the meal to get more?

steps.title: Salt and candle storerooms need checking
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא rules that salt and candle storerooms need בדיקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: A salt storeroom and a candle storeroom need checking.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב הונא adds two more rooms that need checking: where salt is stored and where candles are stored.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During a meal a person might run out of salt or need another candle. He could walk into these rooms while holding bread, so they need checking.

phrases.english: Rabbah bar Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּי מִילְחֵי וּבֵי קִירֵי צָרִיךְ בְּדִיקָה.
phrases.english: A salt storeroom and a candle storeroom need checking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more storerooms to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Salt and candle storerooms need בדיקה.

steps.title: Wood and date storerooms need checking
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that wood and date storerooms need בדיקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: A wood storeroom and a date storeroom need checking.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds two more rooms that need checking: where firewood is kept and where dates are kept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is the same. During a meal a person might need more wood for the fire or more dates to eat, so he might walk in holding bread.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּי צִיבֵי וּבֵי תַמְרֵי צָרִיךְ בְּדִיקָה.
phrases.english: A wood storeroom and a date storeroom need checking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of storerooms.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wood and date storerooms need בדיקה.
steps.whatToRemember: Any room a person might enter during a meal, for salt, candles, wood, dates, small fish, or wine, needs checking.

steps.title: No need to reach into holes and cracks because of danger
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a person is not required to put his hand into holes and cracks to check, because it is dangerous.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: We do not require a person to put his hand into holes and cracks to check, because of the danger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא. A person checking for חמץ does not have to stick his hand into holes and cracks, because that is dangerous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a limit on the duty of בדיקה. The ברייתא does not yet explain what the danger is, and the גמרא will ask about that next.

phrases.english: It was taught:
We do not require him
to put his hand into holes and cracks to check,
because of the danger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new topic: how far a person must go when checking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person is not required to reach into holes and cracks to check for חמץ, because it is dangerous.

steps.title: What danger is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what danger the ברייתא is referring to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What danger?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which danger the ברייתא means. This short question sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only said 'danger' without explaining. Knowing which danger it means will show which holes the ברייתא is talking about.

phrases.english: What danger?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a word in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which danger the ברייתא is referring to.

steps.title: If the danger is a scorpion, how did he ever use the hole?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the danger is a scorpion, then asks how the person ever used that hole if scorpions were a risk.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because of the danger of a scorpion: when he used the hole, how did he use it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests the danger is a scorpion hiding in the hole. Then it pushes back right away: if this is a hole the person uses, he already reaches into it, so it cannot be too dangerous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hole needs checking only if a person uses it and might have put חמץ there. But if he uses it, he already sticks his hand in without fear. So the 'scorpion' reason seems to leave no case for the ברייתא to be talking about.

phrases.english: If you say it is because of the danger of a scorpion,
when he used it, how did he use it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests an answer to the question and immediately challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the ברייתא's danger means a scorpion.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Any hole that needs checking is one the person uses. Since he already reaches into it, it is not dangerous to him.

steps.title: The case is where חמץ fell into the hole
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a hole the person does not use, where חמץ fell in by accident.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for a case where the חמץ fell in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is not talking about a hole the person uses. It is talking about a hole where חמץ happened to fall in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the person never reaches into this hole, a scorpion could really be hiding there. So the ברייתא tells him he does not have to reach in, even though חמץ is inside.

keyTerms.meaning: it is needed only for (the case of)

phrases.english: It is needed only where the חמץ fell in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by defining a new case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case (אוקימתא): חמץ fell by accident into a hole that is not used.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every hole that needs checking is one the person uses, so there is no danger.
steps.terutzMaskana: This hole is not used. חמץ fell into it, and a scorpion could be there.

steps.title: Fallen חמץ should count as destroyed, like חמץ under rubble
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why fallen חמץ needs checking, since a משנה says חמץ buried under rubble counts as destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it fell in, why do I need checking? But we learned in a משנה: חמץ that rubble fell on is considered destroyed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If the חמץ fell into a hole, it should count as gone, just like חמץ that rubble fell on, which a משנה says is treated as destroyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If fallen-in חמץ counts as destroyed, there is nothing to check in the first place. Then the ברייתא would not need to excuse the person because of danger.

phrases.english: If it fell in, why do I need checking?
But we learned:
חמץ that rubble fell on
is considered destroyed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case defined in the previous answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא is about חמץ that fell into a hole.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה teaches that buried חמץ counts as destroyed, so fallen-in חמץ should need no checking at all.

steps.title: Rubble is too deep for a dog, but this hole is not
steps.stepSummary: חמץ under rubble counts as destroyed because a dog cannot dig it out. חמץ in a hole that a dog can reach still needs checking.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is a case where a dog cannot search for it. Here, it is a case where a dog can search for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the difference. The rubble in the משנה buries the חמץ so deep that even a dog cannot reach it, but this hole is shallow enough that a dog could get the חמץ out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חמץ counts as destroyed only if it is buried deeper than a dog could dig. Since a dog could pull the חמץ out of this hole, it is still around and needs to be removed. The person is excused from reaching in only because of the scorpion danger.

keyTerms.meaning: to search for it (dig it out)

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם שֶׁאֵין הַכֶּלֶב יָכוֹל לְחַפֵּשׂ אַחֲרָיו,
phrases.english: There, it is where a dog cannot search for it;
here, it is where a dog can search for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם שֶׁאֵין הַכֶּלֶב יָכוֹל לְחַפֵּשׂ אַחֲרָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by showing how the two cases differ.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Telling apart two cases by how deeply the חמץ is buried.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any חמץ that fell somewhere hard to reach counts as destroyed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only חמץ buried deeper than a dog can dig counts as destroyed. חמץ in a shallow hole still exists, but the person need not reach in because of the scorpion danger.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'dog test': if a dog could dig the חמץ out, it is not considered destroyed.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not say the חמץ in the hole is allowed or destroyed. It still counts as חמץ. The person is only excused from reaching in because of the scorpion danger.
steps.whyThisMatters: The 'dog test' becomes the standard for deciding when buried חמץ counts as destroyed.

steps.title: Why worry about danger? People doing a מצוה are protected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the concern about danger, citing רבי אלעזר's rule that שלוחי מצוה are not harmed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי אלעזר say: people on their way to do a מצוה are not harmed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא worries about danger in the hole at all. רבי אלעזר taught that a person busy with a מצוה will not be harmed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Searching for חמץ is a מצוה. If מצוה-doers are protected, a scorpion in the hole should not be a reason to skip the search. So the ברייתא's concern about danger seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [so-and-so] say? (introduces a challenge from a known statement)
An אמורא whose teaching is quoted here
People sent on, or busy doing, a מצוה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key source for the well-known principle שלוחי מצוה אינן ניזוקין, and this sugya starts to set its limits.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Elazar say:
Those on a מצוה mission are not harmed?
phrases.notes: So why would the ברייתא worry about danger during בדיקת חמץ?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 36 established that the hole must be checked, the גמרא now questions why danger would be a concern there at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's assumption that checking the hole involves danger.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מצוה-doers are protected from harm, so a person checking for חמץ should face no real danger.

steps.title: He might also search for a lost needle
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the person may have lost a needle there and will also look for it, so he is not only doing a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Maybe he lost a needle there, and he will come to look for it as well.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains why the protection does not apply here. The person might also be searching for his own lost needle, not only for חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The protection of שלוחי מצוה applies when a person is busy only with the מצוה. Once he is also looking for his own lost item, his search is partly for himself. So the guarantee of protection may not cover him, and the danger is real again.

keyTerms.meaning: A late אמורא who gives the answer here
To look for it, to search after it

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי does not say the search for חמץ stops being a מצוה. He says it is mixed with a personal goal, and that mix may remove the special protection.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Perhaps he will have lost a needle,
phrases.notes: Lost in that same hole

phrases.english: and he will come to search for it.
phrases.notes: Now his search is not purely for the מצוה

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: שֶׁמָּא תֹּאבַד לוֹ מַחַט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 37 by narrowing when מצוה protection applies.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the person's search is mixed with a personal interest.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every search for חמץ is a pure מצוה, so the searcher is always protected.
steps.terutzMaskana: If he may also look for his lost needle, the search is not purely a מצוה, so the danger still applies.

steps.title: A מצוה with a personal motive is still a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי: even with a personal motive, it should still count as a מצוה, as a ברייתא about charity given for a personal reward shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in a case like this, is it not a מצוה? But it was taught in a ברייתא: One who says, 'This סלע is for charity so that my son will live,' or 'so that I will be part of עולם הבא'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב אשי: a מצוה done with a personal goal should still be a full מצוה. It begins quoting a ברייתא to prove this, and the ברייתא's ruling continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי assumed a personal motive weakens the מצוה. The ברייתא describes someone giving צדקה for a personal reward: his son's life or his own place in עולם הבא. If the ברייתא treats that giving as a full מצוה, then searching for חמץ along with a needle should also be a full מצוה and should be protected.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא? (introduces a challenge from a ברייתא)
A סלע, a type of coin
One who has a share in the World to Come

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא's ruling has not appeared yet. It comes on the next amud, so do not try to finish the proof from this passage alone.

phrases.english: And in a case like this, is it not a מצוה?!
phrases.notes: Rhetorical: of course it should still be a מצוה

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught in a baraita:
One who says: 'This sela is for charity'
'so that my son will live,'
or 'so that I will be one destined for the World to Come' —
phrases.notes: The ruling of the ברייתא continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's answer in step 38 by arguing that a personal motive does not cancel a מצוה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's assumption that a personal interest, like looking for the needle, removes the protection of the מצוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא treats charity given for a personal reward as a מצוה. So a mixed motive should not remove מצוה status, and the searcher should still be protected.
